record.paper_title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry
record.original_question: Let X be an algebraic curve of genus g <= 48 with automorphism group G=Aut(X). Using the subgroup structure of G and the quotient curves X/H, determine all possible isogeny decompositions of the Jacobian Jac(X), especially decompositions into products of Jacobians of quotient curves.

evidence.quote: Let X be a genus g algebraic curve with automorphism group G := Aut (X ).
Problem 10. Using the structure of automorphism groups of algebraic curves of genus g <= 48, determine possible decompositions of Jacobians for these curves.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective algebraic curve over $\mathbb{C}$ of genus $g$ with $2 \le g \le 48$, and let $G = \operatorname{Aut}(X)$ be its full automorphism group. For each subgroup $H \le G$, let $X/H$ denote the quotient curve and $\operatorname{Jac}(X/H)$ its Jacobian. By the Kani–Rosen theorem, idempotent relations in the rational group algebra $\mathbb{Q}[G]$ yield isogeny decompositions of $\operatorname{Jac}(X)$ as products of abelian subvarieties, which in favorable cases are Jacobians of quotient curves $X/H$.

Problem: For every genus $g$ in the range $2 \le g \le 48$ and every group $G$ that occurs as the full automorphism group of some curve $X$ of genus $g$, determine, using the subgroup structure of $G$ and the corresponding quotient curves $X/H$, all possible isogeny decompositions
$$\operatorname{Jac}(X) \sim A_1^{n_1} \times \cdots \times A_k^{n_k},$$
giving in particular all decompositions in which each factor $A_i$ is isogenous to the Jacobian of a quotient curve of $X$ by some subgroup of $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress exists: Kani–Rosen's theorem provides the general framework, and Paulhus and collaborators have developed computational methods (including the "decompose-jacobians" code) that yield decompositions of Jacobians from group/signature data. Full lists of decompositions have been computed in low genus (up to about genus 5–7 and various special families), and ongoing work extends results to larger genus, but a complete classification for all curves with all possible automorphism groups across $2 \le g \le 48$ is not available in the literature, so the problem appears partially solved.

status_evidence.title: decompose-jacobians (Paulhus code)
status_evidence.snippet: Code to decompose Jacobian varieties given a group and a signature acting on a curve. Additionally determines decompositions of Jacobians of intermediate covers given by subgroups of the full automorphism group.
status_evidence.claim: A computational framework exists for systematically computing such decompositions from group-theoretic data.

status_evidence.title: Explicit construction of decomposable Jacobians (thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Jacobian varieties of algebraic curves with many automorphisms provide examples of abelian varieties that contain many factors in their decompositions.
status_evidence.claim: Specific cases and families have been worked out, but the classification is ongoing.

status_evidence.title: Decompositions of Jacobians (arXiv:1807.05270)
status_evidence.snippet: Kani and Rosen proved a decomposition theorem where each factor is isogenous to the Jacobian of a quotient of the curve.
status_evidence.claim: The theoretical foundation (Kani–Rosen) is established and used to produce decompositions in many cases.
